title: [D1 Ingest] Flow record input contract and capture fixtures
summary: `helena.normalizer` now holds the raw flow record contract and the capture registry it is read from. `FlowRecord` is the input exactly as a producer supplies it — 15 Pydantic models, `strict=True` + `extra="forbid"` + `frozen=True`, no identity block — and `as_supplied()` round-trips a parsed record back to its JSON, asserted record by record over all 62 records of `data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl` and both committed capture fixtures. `describe_capture` / `read_capture` / `scan_captures` address a capture by the sha256 of its file, refuse a fixture whose name and content disagree, and refuse a blank line rather than skipping it. Two capture fixtures under `tests/fixtures/captures/`, each named by its own digest, carry every layer combination in the sample plus the absence-is-not-emptiness cases. 116 new tests; the full suite is 291 passed.
assumption_validated: Two, both measured. (1) That the input contract can be written with no invented fields and no identity block, and that the claim is checkable rather than reviewable: `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` equals the parsed JSON for all 62 real records and all 11 fixture records, one test per record — so an invented, dropped, renamed or coerced field is a named failure. Positive. Alongside it, a recursive walk of all 15 models finds no field containing tenant/sensor/schema/capture/raw_record/event_id, and the same walk over the 62 records' JSON keys finds none either: the producer does not send them and the contract has nowhere to put them. (2) That capture identity is provisional while a file is open — appending one record to a described capture changes its hash, its record count and its byte size, and the record already in the file becomes unreadable under the identity it was first described with, while being byte-for-byte the same record. Positive, and it is the demonstration rather than a restatement of the open question. Not validated: nothing has been ingested through this contract, and the requiredness of every field rests on one capture from one host (see `deferred`).
makes_buildable: Task 7 (identity stamping) has the record the identity is stamped onto, and the two halves of a deterministic event id: `Capture.sha256` and the zero-based record offset `read_capture` yields. Task 8 (adapter protocol) has the one format's model to write the first adapter around, and `read_capture` handing over undecoded bytes is the shape a parse failure has to keep. Task 9 (quarantine) has the typed failures to route — `ValidationError` from the contract, `CaptureError` from the registry — and a contract that refuses drift rather than coercing it, so there is something to quarantine. Tasks 10 and 11 have `record_count` and `byte_size` as the reconciliation denominator that the consume-once broker cannot supply, and `scan_captures` as the hash-to-file lookup `helena replay-capture <hash>` needs. Task 12 onward has fixture captures that exercise every layer combination, a null application layer and an empty-but-observed array, so a flatten view can be tested on the case that distinguishes 'no DNS traffic' from 'DNS traffic with no answers'.

verification.detail: 291 passed in 13.8 s, no skips — the integration tests started a throwaway in-memory RisingWave and ran, as before. 116 of the tests are new. `make check` (uv lock --check, compileall, pytest) is green. No SQL was added by this task, so nothing new was executed against the engine; the existing migration and version tests still are. The strict-mode claims in the module docstring were measured against Pydantic 2.13 for both Python objects and JSON input before being written down, and both fixture digests were recomputed with sha256sum outside the test suite.

invariant_conflicts.detail: PRD step 4 says 'implement a capture registry that records file hash, record count and byte size'. The plainest reading — a persisted index of captures — is a second store, which `concept/instruction.md` §2 forbids ('no second database ... no checkpoint store ... no file-backed agent memory'), and an index that disagreed with the files would be worse than no index because the retained files ARE the durable record. Implemented as the compatible half: the registry computes a capture's description by reading it (`describe_capture`), and reads a directory of hash-named files (`scan_captures`). Nothing is written to disk. If a capture ever needs to be citable from a stored row, the row goes in the engine like every other durable row, which is the increment that first writes one — not this one.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: implemented the compatible half; no state file, no index

deferred: The requiredness of every field is derived from one capture — 62 records, one host, 130.8 s — because that is the only flow-record corpus that exists. `data/ingest/README.md` warns explicitly that this capture's ratios describe the capture and not the schema, so a field required here because 15 observations all carried it may be optional in reality, and a producer omitting it will be QUARANTINED rather than accepted. That is the intended direction of the error (drift surfaces, countable, raw record kept), but the quarantine rate is the number to watch when a second capture arrives, and the answer to a high one is a new observation of the input, not a field loosened on a hunch. Rule applied and recorded in docs/decisions/0010: present only if observed; required if present in every observation of its kind; optional if the sample shows it absent at least once, including when the counter-example comes from the other HTTP version.

Cross-field validation that `ip.proto` agrees with which of `tcp`/`udp` is present. True on all 62 records and asserted nowhere, because it is a property of this producer rather than a rule of the input — enforcing it would quarantine the first ICMP record ever sent.

Any interpretation of a value. `ip.src` is a `str`, not an address object; `uri` is the whole URI including the query string, not a host part. Parsing is normalization and belongs to the increments that do it; the host-part rule applies where a domain column is written, not where the record is read.

The adapter protocol, the typed parse-failure envelope and quarantine — tasks 8 and 9. A record that fails validation raises a `ValidationError` and nothing catches it yet; inventing a failure type here would be a contract written ahead of the code that stores it.

Identity stamping, the event id and the schema version — task 7. The schema version is stamped on the normalized event, not on the raw record: the raw record is what arrived and the producer sends no version.

Logging. `helena.observability.logger` needs `Settings` for tenant and sensor, and reading a file to count its records does not need an identity. The increment that consumes the ingest topic already has one.

Streaming reads. `describe_capture` and `read_capture` read the whole file into memory (80 KB for the sample, 11 KB for the fixtures). Fine at fixture scale and premature to change; the increment that replays a large capture should hash in chunks and iterate lines rather than materialise the list.

A malformed-record capture fixture. The contract's rejection paths are tested with records constructed inline from real ones; a committed capture of invalid records belongs to task 9, which is what will have somewhere to put them.
lessons: task 06: `model_dump(exclude_unset=True) == json.loads(line)` over every record of a real capture is the only test that actually demonstrates 'no invented fields' — a field list a human reads cannot fail, and this does, per record, naming the record. Use `exclude_unset` rather than `exclude_none`: the first is a statement about what arrived, the second about what happens to be null now.

task 06: Pydantic 2.13 `strict=True`, measured for both Python objects and `model_validate_json`: `1` into a float field is ACCEPTED (so an integer epoch second still validates), `"1.5"` into a float is rejected, `1.0` into an int is rejected, `True` into an int is rejected, and a string into a str-typed field that arrived as a number is rejected. Strict mode is therefore usable on real telemetry without loosening anything — the one widening it keeps is exactly the one you want.

task 06: `data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl` measured field-by-field: 62 records, top-level keys id/ts/td/ip always, then udp 31, tcp 31, dns 30, tls 25, http2 15, http 11. Six layer combinations occur — dns alone 30, tls+http2 15, http alone 6, tls+http 5, tls alone 5, and ONE record (`udp.28`, SSDP to 239.255.255.250) with no application layer at all. `ip.proto` agrees with which of tcp/udp is present on all 62. Empty-but-observed arrays are real in this data: `tls.csvers` and `tls.ssvers` are empty on almost every TLS observation and `tcp.24` has `tls.alpn == []`. There are no JSON nulls anywhere in the file.

task 06: The HTTP layers differ structurally, not incidentally: `num` and `content_len` appear on HTTP/1 request and response observations and on none of the 21 HTTP/2 requests or 47 HTTP/2 responses. `content_type` and `server` are absent on some HTTP/2 responses and present on all HTTP/1 ones — the same fact over two versions, so they are optional on both. That cross-version counter-example is the only evidence in the sample about which fields are genuinely optional.

task 06: `data/ingest/README.md` is a datasheet holding the sample's sha256, byte size and record count, and it says the checksum IS the version. That makes it a second copy of a constant, so `test_the_sample_capture_matches_its_datasheet` parses those three rows out of the markdown and asserts them against `describe_capture` — the project's 'two copies asserted equal' rule applied to a fixture instead of to a version.

task 06: `tests/test_package_layout.py` uses `rglob("*.py")` and compares file STEMS, so a subpackage (`normalizer/records.py`) fails the layout test on the stem `records`. Everything a component owns goes in its one module file, or `COMPONENT_MODULES`/`SUPPORT_MODULES` has to be edited — which is the intended friction.
failed_approaches: task 06: Asserting in the append-changes-identity test that the first record reads back identically through BOTH the old and the new capture description. `read_capture` re-hashes the file and refuses a description that no longer matches, so the stale one raises `CaptureError` — which is the better demonstration and is what the test now asserts. Worth knowing before writing anything that holds a `Capture` across a write to its file: the description is checked on every read, deliberately.

task 06: `Capture.label` and a `CAPTURE_HASH_ALGORITHM` constant were written and then removed before reporting. Both had exactly one caller — a test — which makes them structure ahead of the increment. The algorithm is named by the field (`sha256`); the regex for a capture filename is built from `CAPTURE_SUFFIX` with `re.escape` so the suffix exists once.
next_session_should_know: `helena.normalizer` is now real and its maturity label is `experimental`. Read a capture through `describe_capture(path)` / `read_capture(capture)` / `scan_captures(directory)` and parse a record with `FlowRecord.model_validate_json(line)` — do not write a second reader, because replay must exercise the same path as live ingestion and a parallel one is what `concept/03-architecture.md` forbids. `read_capture` yields `(offset, raw bytes)` with `offset` the zero-based ordinal in the file and the line undecoded, which is what a quarantine row needs; it re-hashes the file and raises `CaptureError` if the content changed since the `Capture` was described, so do not hold a description across a write. Four things that will bite otherwise. (1) The contract is `strict=True` + `extra="forbid"` + `frozen=True`: any drift — an unknown key, a number sent as a string, a missing field — is a `ValidationError`, and NOTHING catches it yet. Task 8's adapter and task 9's quarantine are what turn it into a typed row; until then a bad record kills the caller. (2) The requiredness of every field comes from one 62-record capture and is the likeliest source of a false quarantine on real traffic — docs/decisions/0010-capture-identity.md has the rule and what to do about a high quarantine rate, and the answer is a new observation of the input, not a loosened field. (3) `as_supplied()` is `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`, and the 62-record round-trip test is what enforces 'no invented fields' — adding a field to any model in the contract will fail 62 tests at once, which is deliberate: a field on the input contract that no producer sends is where a defaulted tenant comes from. (4) Capture identity is the sha256 of the FILE, so the same record in two files belongs to two captures with different references — which is why a raw-record reference is the capture plus an offset and never the record's own `id` (that is the producer's label, `udp.0`/`tcp.17`, unique only within a capture and scoped by protocol). The fixtures are `tests/fixtures/captures/<sha256>.jsonl` with a README mapping each digest to what it holds; every record in them is a byte-for-byte copy of a line of `data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl`, and nothing in them is synthesised on purpose. Still open and untouched by this task: `bin/README.md` still points at a `scripts/build-binaries.sh` that does not exist, and there is still no git repository, so nothing here was committed. The concept/05-vs-data/netify tension that every session from task 0 carried forward is no longer open — `docs/decisions/0009-netify-application-identification.md` settled it by operator decision, so stop reporting it.
